_readme: Migrations whose effects `npm run check:migrations` CANNOT SEE, and where each one stands on prod.
The schema drift check compares live tables and columns. A migration that changes neither — a cron
schedule, a data-only INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, a dropped column, a created or replaced function — is
invisible to it: it reports 'prod in sync' whether or not that migration was ever applied. The miss
is silent in both directions (nothing 500s, no gate turns red, the product renders perfectly), which
is how migration 264 sat outstanding on prod while the check reported green.
`scripts/check-manual-prod-migrations.mjs` derives the CANDIDATE LIST from the migration files
themselves, so a new schema-invisible migration cannot avoid needing an entry here. Declaring one is
a decision point, not paperwork: the session that writes the migration is the session that knows
prod:  applied     confirmed on prod — put the anchor (date / Amplify job) in the note
pending     must be applied at or before the next promote — BLOCKS a promote
held        deliberately not applied, an owner decision — does not block, stays visible
unverified  nobody has checked — BLOCKS a promote; resolving it is a one-minute lookup
grandfatheredThrough: migrations at or below this number predate the gate and are not audited.
Raising it is a deliberate act; lowering it means auditing more history.
